# Work state: your to-do lists and working state
Use claude-mem's work_state_write tool to track all to-do lists and multi-step work. It is your canonical to-do list: use it instead of any built-in to-do tool. Also use it to track the state of anything you need an ongoing understanding of. Whatever is still open is shown here at the start of every session in this project.
- One list per to-do list or tracked thing: work_state_write with list="<name>" and the fields to set
- To-do item: fields {"task": "<name>", "status": "todo" | "doing" | "done" | "dropped", ...any details}
- State: fields {"<key>": <value>} (the latest value of each key wins; null clears a key; "status": "done" closes the list)
- Made something a person can open (PR, deck, page, image, report)? Attach it to that item: fields {"work_product": "https://…" or "/absolute/file"}; several, with titles, as one JSON string: "[{\"title\": \"<name>\", \"url\": \"https://…\"}]"
- Deliverables: write a deck, report, page or other file the person asked for as a file and attach it as work_product before you finish. When you stop, claude-mem copies each attached file (and any deck, document, page, image or spreadsheet you wrote outside the source tree) into this project's deliverables bucket, ~/.claude-mem/deliverables/<project>/, and links it on the request's card in My Work.
- Read every list, closed items included: work_state_read with includeClosed=true

Nothing open yet.

### Nov 3, 2026
5 4:20p ○ cleanDoubleSlashes lacks respectQueryAndFragment; trailing-slash helpers already have it
6 " ○ cleanDoubleSlashes collapses slashes per "://"-delimited segment, with no query or fragment awareness
7 " ○ Existing cleanDoubleSlashes tests live in test/double-slash.test.ts as a table-driven suite
8 " ◆ cleanDoubleSlashes gained an opt-in respectQueryAndFragment flag that leaves the query and hash untouched
9 " ✓ Test suite extended for respectQueryAndFragment; all 13 cleanDoubleSlashes tests pass
S2 Add an opt-in `respectQueryAndFragment` flag to `cleanDoubleSlashes` so `//` inside the query and hash is preserved, with the default behaviour unchanged and tests added. (Nov 3, 4:20 PM)
**Investigated**: The primary session grepped `src`, `docs`, and `README.md` for `cleanDoubleSlashes` and `respectQueryAndFragment`. It read `src/utils.ts` around the trailing-slash helpers and `cleanDoubleSlashes`, and inspected the README section and the existing `test/double-slash.test.ts` table-driven suite.

**Learned**: The trailing-slash helpers (`hasTrailingSlash`, `withoutTrailingSlash`, `withTrailingSlash`) already accept `respectQueryAndFragment` and split off the query and fragment before editing. `cleanDoubleSlashes` had no such option. It splits on `://` and collapses every slash run in each segment, so `//` inside a query such as `?redirect=//baz` gets collapsed. That is the source of the redirect-target bug.

**Completed**: `cleanDoubleSlashes(input, respectQueryAndFragment?)` is implemented in `src/utils.ts`. With `true`, it cleans only the part before the first `?` or `#` and reattaches the rest unchanged. The JSDoc and the README entry were updated to describe the flag. Seven opt-in test cases and one default-behaviour test were added to `test/double-slash.test.ts`. `vitest` passes all 13 tests in that file, and `tsc --noEmit` printed no errors. Changes are not committed.

**Next Steps**: Nothing is in progress. The remaining open item is running the wider test suite beyond `test/double-slash.test.ts`, which has not been done yet.

**Notes**: The edits to `src/utils.ts` and the README were applied with Python string replacement, which fails silently on a non-matching pattern. The passing test run is what confirms the new branch is actually in place. Prettier was also run on `src/utils.ts` and the test file, so formatting changes outside the functional edit are possible.
